absent: Raw atomic operation effects, return values and ordering guarantees beyond width dispatch and instrumentation layering.
Futex wait, wake, requeue, priority-inheritance and hash lookup behavior beyond identity, state and inline lifecycle helpers.
Underlying per-CPU local-lock primitives, interrupt handling and bottom-half nesting effects beyond wrapper delegation.
Preemption, bit operation, lock dependence, race-detector and instrumentation internals owned by other dossiers.
Robust list traversal, compat translation and vDSO critical-section fixup targets beyond range containment and setter behavior.

findings.text: Long conditional decrement operations select between wide and narrow raw implementations according to build word size, with the instrumented decrement-if-positive form applying race-detector and access handling before reaching raw logic.

Exchange operations exist in default, acquire, release and relaxed ordering flavours, each accepting a target location plus caller operands and forwarding to a matching raw operation after instrumentation handling.

Compare-and-exchange interfaces cover normal, 64-bit and 128-bit widths, each with default, acquire, release, relaxed and CPU-local flavours plus a synchronizing form, forwarding to corresponding raw primitives after instrumentation.

Boolean try-compare-exchange interfaces add an expected-value location beside the target, spanning normal, 64-bit and 128-bit widths with default, acquire, release, relaxed, CPU-local and synchronizing flavours, instrumenting both locations before delegating to raw peers.
The long atomic holder, its initializer and its conditional-read helpers alias to the 64-bit family on wide builds and to the plain integer family otherwise.

Default and synchronizing instrumented forms include a full race-detector barrier and release forms include a release marker, while acquire, relaxed and CPU-local forms omit race-detector barriers but still record atomic access.

Single-bit spin acquisition disables preemption, then where multiprocessor or debug support exists retries an acquiring test-and-set with non-atomic polling pauses while contended; otherwise it relies on preemption control alone.

Single-bit try acquisition disables preemption and makes one acquiring attempt where supported, restoring preemption and reporting failure on contention and otherwise claiming ownership and reporting success.

Both single-bit release forms check ownership under debug builds, clear the bit with unlock ordering where supported using ordered versus unchecked clearing respectively, then re-enable preemption and drop lock context.
Single-bit locked query inspects the bit where multiprocessor or debug support exists, otherwise reports preemption nesting where counted, and otherwise reports a constant locked indication.
Bit-lock dependence tracking derives its lock identity from the pairing of bit index with word address.

Futex identity is a union with shared, private and combined views holding sequence, address, page, offset and node related members, where the combined node member is documented as excluded from hashing.
Futex key reference flags use first value for inode linkage and second value for shared address-space linkage.
The default futex key constant is the union value whose combined pointer component is zero.
Maximum robust unlock ranges equals one, plus one more when compat handling is enabled.
Per-task futex lifecycle exposes three states corresponding to healthy, exiting and dead.
Task futex setup clears the per-task futex area, prepares its inheritance state list, marks healthy state and initializes its exit serialization mutex.
Scheduler-visible futex state groups native and compat robust list pointers, an inheritance state list, a cached inheritance state, an exit mutex and a state word.
Private futex hash control for an address space either holds a mutex, RCU hash pointers, batch count, callback head, atomic counter and per-CPU reference, or is empty when disabled.
Robust unlock range records a start address, length and operand-size flag, with per-address-space storage sized by the configured maximum or empty when unsupported.
Per-address-space futex data combines private hash control with robust unlock ranges when enabled, and is empty otherwise.
Scheduler and address-space futex holders and unlock-range holders collapse to empty structures under configurations without futex or robust unlock support.
Shown hash lifecycle helpers report success without action, while disabled task lifecycle helpers are no-ops and disabled main and hash control entries report invalid-argument failure.

Robust unlock support offers a containment test for an instruction pointer inside a recorded range, a fixup walk over configured ranges gated on interrupt-return state, a setter deriving length from bounds plus operand size, and no-op forms plus empty address-space init where unsupported.

Per-CPU local locking exposes init, lock, interrupt-disabling lock, flag-saving lock, unlock, interrupt-restoring unlock, try-lock, interrupt-aware try-lock, locked query and nested bottom-half pairs, each resolving the calling CPU instance before delegating inward.
Scoped guard constructors bind local lock, interrupt, flag-saving, nested bottom-half and init operations to generic with-guard construction.
Local lock context optionally carries dependence tracking and ownership, while try-lock context adds an acquisition flag; both expose distinct type aliases.
Debug acquisition for local locks performs exclusive dependence acquisition, warns on existing ownership and records the current task, with the try form using a try-acquisition marker instead.
Debug builds treat releasing a clear bit-lock as a fatal ownership violation, so callers must only release bits they hold.
Try-compare-exchange forms instrument both the target word and the expected-value holder, so callers must supply a valid writable expected location with a role distinct from the target.
Mutex initialization creates a per-call-site lock class key and forwards identity and key to the underlying initializer inside a single-statement wrapper.
